title: Binary Tree Boundary Values
statement:
List the values on the outside edge of a binary tree in counter-clockwise order.

Contract
- `root` may be null. Return an empty list for an empty tree.
- For a non-empty tree, return the root, then the left boundary excluding leaves, then all leaves left to right, then the right boundary excluding leaves in bottom-up order.
- A single-node tree returns that one value once. Do not duplicate leaves or mutate the tree.

Examples
`boundaryValues(tree(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7))` => `[1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 3]`
`boundaryValues(tree(1, null, 2, 3, 4))` => `[1, 3, 4, 2]`
`boundaryValues(null)` => `[]`
hints: Separate the outside into left edge, leaves, and right edge.
Leaves belong to the leaf phase, so skip them when collecting the side boundaries.
Collect the right boundary top-down into a temporary list, then append it reversed. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(h) extra stack space plus the result.
inputSyntax: Input: the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
